issue_context.title: Device doesn't support requested value
issue_context.body:
On Hassio 0.94.x the emulated hue component is not working properly, regarding the last Amazon Alexa app version.

On the device list, the alexa app reports errors on every single light device reported by emulated_hue: "Device doesn't support requested value".

Neither is possible to create routines involving the brightness of those lights, as the screen for setting that appears completely blank.

It is possible to power on and off the lights through voice commands on the echo dot 3.

supports your lamp brightness?

@croghostrider, Nop. I'm on 0.97.2 right now and the issue remains.
I still have the same issue with Hass.io 188 with version 0.99.2

Same problem here. Started two or three weeks ago (possibly after adding a new Echo Dot 3rd gen).

- Upgraded from `0.93` to `0.99.1`
- Changed the `emulated_hue` port from the default to `80`

The last change made all devices change state in the alexa to `Device doesn't support requested value`.
Trying to turn a light on makes it turn on and immediately off again.

Screenshot from the alexa app (in German):
![](https://ds.ulo.pe/0MpeQCIdP8.jpeg)
Lets see if https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/pull/26541 would solve this issue, or not.

@tiagofreire-pt, I copied the hue_api.py into my virtual_env (not the cleanest way to try, but it seems to work and I don't want to rummage through several versions of breaking changes right now...), and my dimmers and RGBW lights still show "Device doesn't support requested value". My switches now show up as switches (believe before they showed up as having a level setting).

I might try 512759d in earnest if I can find the time.

> I might try [512759d](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/commit/512759dbacd232d00abfa996bc9eac5847a5cde5) in earnest if I can find the time.

Yeah, same problem.

Running a fresh test install of 0.100.2, and the issue is still present. Prepare yourself - I wasted hours on this (but learned a lot) so I figured I'd let you join my adventure. In the end, my issue may be different from that of others, but hopefully I can shed some light into how things work and if there are still issues for others, they can see things in a new light when troubleshooting.
 

### # Root Cause Analysis
Looking into this in __much__ greater depth, I found that the issue is _"caused by"_ [hue_api.py:288-366](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/emulated_hue/hue_api.py#L288-L366), which handles requests to get/set info about entities. I quoted that for reasons I'll discuss momentarily. The pertinent code doesn't have an `elif` for the _group_ domain (for my own specific case; possibly different domains for others), which results in the data massaging performed for entities of the specified domains (_light_, _script_, _climate_, _media_player_, _cover_, and _fan_) to never happen; thus values for _hue_ and _saturation_ are left as _None_. I tracked this down by adding a _logging_ message directly after [hue_api.py:573](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/emulated_hue/hue_api.py#L573):
```
574:    _LOGGER.warn('nam: %s, dom: %s, on: %s, bri: %s, hue: %s, sat: %s', config.get_entity_name(entity), entity.domain, state[STATE_ON], state[STATE_BRIGHTNESS], state[STATE_HUE], state[STATE_SATURATION])
```

Resultant output:
```
2019-10-17 01:34:14 WARNING (MainThread) [custom_components.emulated_hue.hue_api] nam: Computer Room Lights, dom: group, on: True, bri: 0, hue: None, sat: None
```

Bingo!! Now that we know _why_ Alexa isn't happy, let's see if there's anything we can do, such as injecting "fake" data to make her happy. I attempted to further pick this apart by importing the _group_ component and inserted the following code at [hue_api.py:368](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/emulated_hue/hue_api.py#L368):
```
11:    group,
...
368:        # FIXME: If the entity is a group, insert some fake data
369:        elif entity.domain == group.DOMAIN:
370:            domain = entity.domain
371:            data[ATTR_BRIGHTNESS] = 10
372:
```

This, however, results in an error due to _group_ domain entities not accepting the _brightness_ attribute.
```
2019-10-17 03:44:59 ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant.core] Error doing job: Task exception was never retrieved
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/core.py", line 1211, in async_call
    processed_data = handler.schema(service_data)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.7/site-packages/voluptuous/schema_builder.py", line 272, in __call__
    return self._compiled([], data)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.7/site-packages/voluptuous/schema_builder.py", line 594, in validate_dict
    return base_validate(path, iteritems(data), out)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.7/site-packages/voluptuous/schema_builder.py", line 432, in validate_mapping
    raise er.MultipleInvalid(errors)
voluptuous.error.MultipleInvalid: extra keys not allowed @ data['brightness']
```

Fine, fine; I suppose _group_ wasn't really meant to be passed to emulated Hue. But A+ for that validation! I'll use _[light.group](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/light.group/)_ instead. _(which, before today, I wasn't aware existed...)_
 

### # Other findings
Aside from all of this, I found some room for improvement with how [hue_api.py:571-596](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/emulated_hue/hue_api.py#L571-L596) performs its device checks:
```
def entity_to_json(config, entity, state):
    """Convert an entity to its Hue bridge JSON representation."""
    entity_features = entity.attributes.get(ATTR_SUPPORTED_FEATURES, 0)
    if (entity_features & SUPPORT_BRIGHTNESS) or entity.domain != light.DOMAIN:
        return {
            "state": {
                HUE_API_STATE_ON: state[STATE_ON],
                HUE_API_STATE_BRI: state[STATE_BRIGHTNESS],
                HUE_API_STATE_HUE: state[STATE_HUE],
                HUE_API_STATE_SAT: state[STATE_SATURATION],
                "reachable": True,
            },
            "type": "Dimmable light",
            "name": config.get_entity_name(entity),
            "modelid": "HASS123",
            "uniqueid": entity.entity_id,
            "swversion": "123",
        }
    return {
        "state": {HUE_API_STATE_ON: state[STATE_ON], "reachable": True},
        "type": "On/off light",
        "name": config.get_entity_name(entity),
        "modelid": "HASS321",
        "uniqueid": entity.entity_id,
        "swversion": "123",
    }
```

To simplify, the `or entity.domain != light.DOMAIN` check results in every non- _light_ domain entity (fans, covers, etc) to always appear to Alexa as a simple dimmable light. That's fine, I suppose, but there could (and should) be more checks for types of lights with additional capabilities (Color Light, Extended Color Light, and Color Temperature Light). _(More on this below, in the referenced commit.)_
 

### # Regarding the proposed commit
> I might try [512759d](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/commit/512759dbacd232d00abfa996bc9eac5847a5cde5) in earnest if I can find the time.

This worked for me, as the logic issue found in my second point has been adjusted to fall back to a plain "On/off light" for devices that don't support any light-like features. For my own case, this is fine since I really just need to be able to turn a room "on" or "off". Two minor nitpicks, but nothing to sweat over:
1. In keeping with conventions, [hue_api.py:617](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/blob/512759dbacd232d00abfa996bc9eac5847a5cde5/homeassistant/components/emulated_hue/hue_api.py#L617) should read "HASS231"; the second "S" is absent in this commit.
2. I don't know that the _unique_id_ stuff is necessary; removing it while testing everything I tested today caused no issue, and its inclusion is unclear; I'm not currently familiar enough with the protocol to know if there was a reason it was added to begin with. _(perhaps it was done for testing purposes, or to prevent some form of entity id collisions?)_

That said, I do believe this commit is a great addition to the _emulated_hue_ component, as it fills the gaps left for other types of non-plug lights (Color Light, Extended Color Light, and Color Temperature Light), so :thumbsup: to that! I'd very much like to see this commit merged into HA.
 

### # Lessons learned
1. HA does good validation when you try to do things you shouldn't. Don't do things you shouldn't.
2. [light.group](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/light.group/)s are your friend. [group](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/group/)s should not be used directly with _emulated_hue_.
3. I have so much more to learn. :stuck_out_tongue_winking_eye:
 

\- NobleKangaroo

Interesting.

The devices where I still get the error with [512759d](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/commit/512759dbacd232d00abfa996bc9eac5847a5cde5), are--I believe--in the light domain. Three dimmable and one RGBW, more specifically:
two lamp dimmers with `supported_features: 49`, which indicates `SUPPORT_BRIGHTNESS`, `SUPPORT_COLOR`, `SUPPORT_TRANSITION` are set.
one dimmer switch with `supported_features: 33`, which indicates `SUPPORT_BRIGHTNESS`,  `SUPPORT_TRANSITION` are set.
and a RGBW LED strip with `supported_features: 51`, which indicates `SUPPORT_BRIGHTNESS`, `SUPPORT_COLOR_TEMP`,  `SUPPORT_COLOR` and `SUPPORT_TRANSITION` are set.

Working entities are a cover, and three switches.

I plan to do some more digging when I have some free time this weekend.

I haven't gotten a chance to look into this, but the above referenced PR should fix it: https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/pull/28317

I may get a chance over the next weekend, or during the Thanksgiving holiday to give that a shot and report back.

Hi @kvermilion,

Yes my PR #28317 fixes this (#25047) and other issues (including #23514 and #26425). As to **why** this happens, see my previous findings [above](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/issues/25047#issuecomment-543063968).

Regarding [PR 512759d](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/commit/512759dbacd232d00abfa996bc9eac5847a5cde5)), there's a few things in that commit that "bother" me:
- Response codes and patterns inconsistent - I've cleaned this up to return 401 (unauthorized) when appropriate, and return all responses the same way
- Device `uniqueid` values don't match Hue conventions (should start with 00: else Alexa doesn't find devices when discovering)
- General code cleanups

I've used my own modified Emulated Hue for the last month or so and had nothing but good things to report - no more errors, devices are discovering, and color control from the Alexa app is 100% functional.

I'm hoping to see my PR accepted, or at least some feedback provided if there's something I need to improve.

in case anyone else runs into the same thing, my on/off switches were no longer discovered by alexa after upgrading to 0.103.0 (which includes PR #28317). the fix was to change the emulated hue port from 8300 to 80 in my config. after that (and along the way removing emulated_hue_ids.json), everything was discovered properly. now those devices properly show up as on/off devices rather than dimmable bulbs. color support now too, woohoo. my guess is that alexa falls back to an older hue protocol/api version when the port != 80.

> in case anyone else runs into the same thing, my on/off switches were no longer discovered by alexa after upgrading to 0.103.0 (which includes PR #28317). the fix was to change the emulated hue port from 8300 to 80 in my config. after that (and along the way removing emulated_hue_ids.json), everything was discovered properly. now those devices properly show up as on/off devices rather than dimmable bulbs. color support now too, woohoo. my guess is that alexa falls back to an older hue protocol/api version when the port != 80.

Hi tofurky,

Any chance you could test that port (now that you've reset emulated_hue_ids) and see if it works? I don't have that ability to do so ATM but would be good to know if changing the port outright breaks things (and ultimately possibly provide room for future fixes/growth to support that).

Edit: I may also have to tinker with the official Hue bridge and see what, if anything, is different (and why) when you use a port other than 80. Seems very peculiar that things would just break. Ultimately, however, [the only official port that the Hue bridge is *supposed* to be listening on is 80](http://www.hueproapp.com/support.php#question1_8) so I'm not entirely convinced a lot of attention would be be needed, unless Hue agree that Alexa and Google should play nicely with alternate port, which would put the ball back in their courts if they don't currently do so. Thoughts?

Thanks, and happy holidays!

> Any chance you could test that port (now that you've reset emulated_hue_ids) and see if it works? I don't have that ability to do so ATM but would be good to know if changing the port outright breaks things (and ultimately possibly provide room for future fixes/growth to support that).

i'm able to consistently reproduce this by forgetting all devices in alexa, stopping homeassistant, removing emulated_hue_ids.json, changing port 80 <-> 8300, starting home assistant, and rediscovering via alexa.

i did run into a weird caching issue where after once going from 80 -> 8300, the on/off devices (shown as "Royal Philips Electronics smart device" in alexa) were still "rediscovered", but none of them were controllable. alexa said they were offline.

the caching was such that i could forget all devices, stop home assistant (and not start it back up), and rediscover - they'd all show back up. another time, all the id's were mixed up, so i could tell alexa to control one light but the command would go to another.

it was either rebooting all my echos, or forgetting the devices one by one at alexa.amazon.com rather than "forget all", which finally cleared the cache.

but yeah, once i fixed the caching issue, port :8300 consistently did not pick up the on/off devices, whereas port :80 did. alexa is pretty much a black box, especially how it does hue discovery. shrug.

>  port :8300 consistently did not pick up the on/off devices, whereas port :80 did
I haven't been able to get it working with port 8300 for several months now. It now seems to be a limitiation in the alexa implementation itself.

> I haven't been able to get it working with port 8300 for several months now. It now seems to be a limitiation in the alexa implementation itself.

i have older gen echos which still somewhat work on non-standard ports. anyways, i've been on port 80 since i made my original reply and it's working OK.
